caption:
"Treat women nicely, for a woman is created from a rib, and the most curved portion of the rib is its upper portion..."

Sahih al-Bukhari 3331 - part of the Prophet's ﷺ own guidance on how a man should be with his wife. Swipe for Arabic, English, Mandarin, Korean, Japanese and Malay.

Sources on the final slide.

sourcing.primary_text: Sahih al-Bukhari 3331, narrated by Abu Huraira - built for the requested topic 'how exactly should a man be with his new family, i.e. wife, children.' The Prophet's ﷺ own instruction ('Treat women nicely... So treat women nicely') is the primary teaching, framed with the rib metaphor as an illustration of patience with a spouse's nature rather than trying to forcibly change her.
sourcing.arabic_and_english: Live-fetched and independently verified this session (2026-09-18) via mcp__workspace__web_fetch of https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3331 (HTTP 200), Prophets chapter, In-book reference: Book 60, Hadith 6, USC-MSA reference: Vol. 4, Book 55, Hadith 548. Arabic and English quoted verbatim from that page. Per this channel's methodology, the WebSearch AI-summary that first surfaced this reference was NOT trusted on its own - the actual sunnah.com page was fetched directly to confirm the exact wording before use.
sourcing.grade: No separate Grade box is shown on sunnah.com for Sahih al-Bukhari hadith (Bukhari's collection carries inherent authenticity status by scholarly consensus, unlike the Sunan collections which sunnah.com grades individually, e.g. Darussalam/Al-Albani gradings).
sourcing.chinese_korean_japanese_malay: hadith-api (cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/fawazahmed0/hadith-api) has NO Chinese, Korean, Japanese, or Malay editions for any hadith collection, confirmed via its editions.json this session. Per the channel's established convention for this gap (already used for nawawi-13, nawawi-15, bukhari-1-1), these four language slides are Claude's own careful translation, produced directly from the verified Arabic and English sunnah.com text above, and labelled on-slide as such rather than credited to a named translator or scholar who did not produce them.
